findings.title: Lists tab Delete acts on the Library-rail collection, not the collection highlighted in the Lists rail
findings.evidence: Runtime probe P3 (synthetic-probe-result-20261016T110051.json): Lists rail highlighted id 2 (Y list); Collections.SelectedCollection id 1 (X list); ListMemberTiles ids [1,2] (X members); clicking Lists Delete issued DeleteCollectionAsync for id 1. Code: the new Library rail writes Collections.SelectedCollection and navigates to the Lists tab (LibraryView.cs:249-251); ListsView syncs only from its own rail SelectionChanged (ListsView.cs:48-60), does not observe SelectedCollection (OnHostChanged ListsView.cs:290-320), and Delete deletes SelectedCollection immediately with no confirmation (ListsView.cs:174-182). SelectedCollection writers in src: LibraryView.cs:249 (new), ListsView.cs:54, Xbox ListsPage.xaml.cs:271.
findings.rationale: The port added a second desktop writer of the shared collection selection without updating the Lists tab, so an unconfirmed, irreversible server-side delete can target a collection the Lists tab does not highlight. Main had no such path. The Library rail item also stays selected, so choosing the same collection again does not navigate again.
findings.correction: Keep one selection source: have ListsView observe Collections.SelectedCollection and select the matching rail row (or route Library-rail navigation through a VM command that ListsView consumes); make Delete act on the visibly highlighted row (disable it when they differ) and confirm before deleting. Write a headless contract test reproducing P3 first (mock gate, then production binding).

findings.title: Returning to the Library tab drops the selected game, disables Attach and rebuilds the cover loader and cache
findings.evidence: Probes P2 and P2b (new view, both construction orders): before the tab switch gridSelectedIndex 3, SelectedGroup Game 0004, CanAttach true; detached while on the other tab; after return gridSelectedIndex -1, SelectedGroup null, CanAttach false, new loader instance. Baseline P5 (main fa259f2 LibraryView in the same harness): selection 3, Game 0004 and CanAttach true preserved after return. Code: OnAttachedToVisualTree runs RebuildCoverLoader and BindList (ItemsSource null, then Items); OnDetachedFromVisualTree disposes the loader and clears _boundBrowse; the cleared ListBox selection now writes SelectedGroup = null. Library shares the sidebar TabControl with Peripherals, Settings, Monitor, History, Lists and CSDb (AttachPanelView.cs:108-130), and a new CoverCache refetches every realized cover.
findings.rationale: Functional regression against main in a common flow (select a game, attach, check Peripherals or Lists, return) that the new Library rail itself triggers by navigating to Lists. No test covers it.
findings.correction: Rebind only when Browse actually changed; keep the loader for the lifetime of the Browse instance (dispose on Browse change or host disposal rather than every visual detach) or restore selection and detail on re-attach. Add a headless test first: select, switch tab, return, then assert selection, CanAttach and loader identity are preserved.

findings.title: Cover grid is not virtualized: every loaded tile is realized and loads and holds a full-resolution cover, so the claimed off-screen fix is unsupported
findings.evidence: Avalonia 12.0.5 metadata: Avalonia.Controls.WrapPanel derives from Panel, not VirtualizingPanel, and Avalonia.Controls 12.0.5 has no virtualizing wrap panel. Probe P1: ItemsPanel WrapPanel, itemsPanelIsVirtualizing false; 60 items gave 60 realized tile images with 6 inside the viewport; after two Load more pages 180 items gave 180 realized. Baseline P5 (main grid): VirtualizingStackPanel with 8 realized containers for 60 items. Each realized tile starts a cover load on attach (LibraryView.cs:389-394); covers decode at full resolution (new Bitmap(stream)); CoverCache keeps all bytes; BindList after Load more, A-Z, Recents or tab return recreates all tiles and decodes every cover again.
findings.rationale: The record says the old loader could retain off-screen loads and that LibraryCoverImage corrected it. With a non-virtualizing panel, off-screen tiles never detach, so the off-screen cancellation in LibraryCoverImage (its summary cites AC-COVER-03) never runs for scrolled-away tiles. Memory and fetch volume grow with every loaded page (60 per page): a scalability regression against the virtualized list in main. FR-ROMM-COVER-001 describes large virtualized grids.
findings.correction: Use a virtualizing layout for tiles (for example rows of tiles in a VirtualizingStackPanel, or a vetted virtualizing wrap panel), or bound realized and decoded covers (Bitmap.DecodeToWidth plus eviction). Correct the LibraryCoverImage summary and the record claim. Add a test that realized tiles stay bounded by the viewport, or get explicit operator acceptance of the limitation.
